decision: Compare every captured column of retained post-bootstrap CDC images before considering cleanup
scope: Read-only value reconciliation; no cleanup executor or change to archive/warehouse contracts
decisions: Discover the captured columns and their SQL types for all six configured capture instances. Read every captured value from the retained change table, including before/after update images, within the fixed observation boundary.
Preserve NULL explicitly in source JSON and reject missing or additional archive fields. A new unsupported SQL type fails closed rather than being silently dropped.

Serialize exact numerics as text at the source and compare using Decimal without context-dependent rounding. Preserve integer precision beyond 2^53 and all seven fractional timestamp digits. Do not trim strings, normalize Unicode or convert exact values through floating point.

For the existing Debezium isostring configuration, normalize the connector's date/timestamp Z suffix against SQL timezone-free values without using Python microsecond datetime conversion. Unknown timezone-bearing types are not accepted by this mapping.

Compare geography/geometry as native SQL Server serialized bytes, matching the observed connector bytes representation. Do not replace it with WKB, which would alter the representation and discard native metadata.
Use a multiset of canonical value hashes per retained CDC image identity, preserving multiplicity. Report only counts, hashes and differing column names, never business values.
Reobserve source values and captured metadata after the archive scan. Changes inside the same bounded observation invalidate source stability.
Check captured-column sets in snapshot envelopes, but do not call this full source snapshot value reconciliation. Explicitly report tables without retained CDC images.
Treat SQL CDC unavailable-value NULL representations as captured data. Do not manufacture older values from the current base table.

Record the CDC update mask. Diagnose the pinned Debezium 3.7.0 unavailable-value rule only for an unchanged large-object column with source NULL, an update operation and the exact expected marker. Keep strict equality false for these cells; diagnostic representation consistency is not proof of preserved original values.
Keep all existing independent cleanup gates and the unconditional prohibition on audit-authorized deletion. Retain v1 evidence and the prior image for rollback.
limits: The 100,000-row-per-capture bound and 512 MiB one-off container remain lab constraints. Row width and archive size can also limit this implementation; larger histories need partitioned reconciliation and measured capacity.
Unsupported types, including float/real, datetimeoffset and arbitrary user-defined types, require a reviewed mapping before use. Type support is deliberately explicit.
Matching captured values cannot recover data SQL CDC did not retain, prove transaction atomicity, certify a durable connector offset, or authorize retirement of any application.

Marker treatment requires a separate, versioned consumer/reconstruction contract. No raw event, source row or existing warehouse semantic hash is rewritten by this audit. A marker must not silently replace a known business value or be treated as SQL NULL.
Complete source observations contain business values and are protected inputs; they must not be copied into the repository or public acceptance reports.
Single-VM durability, recovery, retention approval, other CDC consumers and pre-bootstrap history remain separate unresolved concerns.
